name: Mokokchung Town
description: District headquarters and cultural capital of the Ao Naga tribe, perched at 1,325 m with misty hills, markets, and panoramic views. Known as the Land of Pioneers.
facts: Elevation about 1,325 m above sea level
Cultural nerve centre of Ao people

name: Ungma Village
description: Oldest and one of the largest Ao Naga villages, just south of Mokokchung town, with historic log drums, Baptist church, and living traditions. Believed to be an early settlement of the Ao people.
facts: One of the oldest Ao settlements

name: Longkhum Village
description: Highest Ao village at about 1,846 m, known as the Vegetable Capital of Nagaland. Offers rhododendron forests, Mata Yimkong viewpoint, stone bridge, and soul-retaining folklore with panoramic valley views.
facts: Highest altitude village in Ao region (~1846 m)

name: Mopungchuket Village
description: Cleanest and popular rural tourism village of Ao Nagas, featuring Jina-Etiben love towers, Süngkotenem Park with mystical lake, wooden sculptures, museum, and log drums. Declared rural tourism village in 2007.
facts: Associated with Romeo-Juliet legend of Jina and Etiben
Features community park and oldest village museum

name: Chuchuyimlang Village
description: Largest Ao village and key site for Moatsu Festival celebrations, known for inviting neighboring tribes. Cultural hub with traditional gatherings and handicrafts, about 30 km from town.
facts: One of the largest Ao villages
On NH-61 about 30 km from Mokokchung

name: Langpangkong Caves
description: Limestone caves in the Langpangkong range between Dikhu and Tzula river valleys, near Changtongya and Tuli. Legend of Ahom king taking refuge; suitable for trekking and exploration.
facts: Associated with Ahom king refuge legend
Coordinates approximate; Sources: tourism guides, district sites

name: Mokokchung District Museum
description: Museum in Mokokchung town showcasing Ao Naga artefacts including weapons, jewelry, clothing, traditional tools, and cultural exhibits from the district.
facts: Preserves Ao tribal artefacts and history

name: Ao Baptist Church (Baptist Mother Church)
description: One of the largest and historically significant Baptist churches in Nagaland, central to Ao Naga Christian life and literacy history in Mokokchung town.
facts: Nicknamed Ao Baptist Church or Mokokchung Church

name: Mokokchung Park
description: Town park above the center of Mokokchung offering green space, gardens, viewpoints, and a quiet break amid the hills. Ideal for walks and picnics.
facts: Also known as Town Park or Fazl Ali Park

name: Dikhu River (Mokokchung section)
description: Scenic river flowing through eastern Mokokchung, ideal for picnics, fishing, and nature walks. Forms part of the district's landscape and boundaries.
facts: Also known as Tzula or Tsula in parts
Coordinates approximate for section; Sources: tourism guides

name: Wokha Town
description: District headquarters and cultural heart of the Lotha Naga tribe, at about 1,313 m elevation. Known as the Land of Plenty, with markets, churches, and views of surrounding hills.
facts: HQ of Wokha district, Lotha heartland

name: Mount Tiyi
description: Highest peak in Wokha district at about 1,969 m, known as the Mountain of Life. Sacred to Lotha Nagas with folklore of an invisible orchard and abode of departed souls. Offers trekking, rhododendrons, and panoramic views.
facts: Coordinates approximate; Sources: wokha.nic.in, tourism guides

name: Doyang Hydro Project and Reservoir
description: 75 MW hydroelectric dam and the largest reservoir in Nagaland on the Doyang River, about 38 km from Wokha. Famous for scenic views, water sports potential, and as a key roosting area for migratory Amur falcons.

name: Pangti Village
description: Lotha Naga village near Doyang Reservoir, known as the Amur Falcon Capital of the World. Hosts the largest annual gathering of migratory Amur falcons (October-November). Community-led conservation success story.
facts: Amur Falcon Capital of the World
Peak viewing mid-Oct to early Nov

name: Mount Totsu and Totsu Cliff
description: Second highest peak area in the district at about 1,250 m, with dramatic cliff offering panoramic valley views. Folklore of giant snake and crab guardians; popular for rock climbing and trekking, about 25 km from Wokha.
facts: Coordinates approximate; Sources: tourism guides, wokha.nic.in

name: Liphanyan Governor's Camp
description: Scenic campsite on the foothills near the Doyang River, about 43-45 km from Dimapur. Ideal for picnics, angling, rafting, and nature walks with river and forest views.
facts: Coordinates approximate; Sources: Incredible India, tourism sites

name: Vankhosung
description: Village about 2-4 km north of Wokha town at the foothills of Mount Tiyi. Site of the first American Baptist Mission activity in the area starting in 1923, with historic mission compound and scenic surroundings.
facts: Birthplace of Christianity in Wokha area
